expected: In 1937, early LEGO risked a fortune on specialized manufacturing machinery. Founder Ole Kirk Kristiansen bought a German wood milling spindle machine. It cost four thousand kroner, one third of their yearly profit. That same amount could buy a complete family house back then. Carpenters previously cut wooden toys using manual rough coping hand saws. The machine milled rounded child-safe edges, vastly accelerating toy workshop production.
